scope: Level 02 art: four stele bases, the rotating ring, three cranks, the gate leaf in both states with its latch, four dark mouths (P0); the grove floor, three axle bars, three crank match marks, the sleeping hollow with its fireflies, Lumo's grass bell and the flying-firefly frames (P1/P2).
style: Painterly pixel-cluster fantasy RPG, front-facing orthographic top-down view with a slight visible top face, cold blue-grey slate, dark teal moss, old honey brass, soft upper-left light. Follows the Level 01 V4 direction (assets/levels/01-forgotten-forest-edge/v4/ART-DIRECTION.md).

revisions.reason: The first sheet filled the stele face with the glyph, so the rotating ring covered it. Regenerated with the glyph at about 40 percent of the face width and a wide blank stone border for the ring to sit around.

In the first sheet the cranks were post-and-wheel scenes; at 16x16 the shaped hub disappeared. Regenerated as face-on wheels with a large bright hub, and the hub mark is stamped at 1x by prepare-assets.py because a downscaled painting cannot stay legible at that size.

prompts.sheet: 1536x1024, 1 row x 4 cells (only the ring cell is used)
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY FOUR isolated mechanism sprites in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, very generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor, shadow or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
Cell 1: the ROTATING RING that sits over a stele face, reading at 28x28 logical pixels but drawn large. A thin worn honey-brass ring with a hollow FULLY TRANSPARENT centre, one raised rectangular NOTCH tab on the top edge, two small rivets, dark patina in the recess. The ring must read as a rim that turns in 120-degree steps; it is not a solid disc and carries no glyph.
Cells 2 to 4: three CRANK wheels that stand on the forest floor, each reading at 16x16 logical pixels but drawn large, each with the SAME body: a short dark wooden post, a small brass axle, a flat round wheel face with a worn rim and a low handle knob at the side. Same size, baseline and lighting in all three; ONLY the shaped hub at the centre differs so the three are told apart by silhouette, never by colour:
cell 2 hub is TWO CROSSED BARS forming an X;
cell 3 hub is a THREE-PRONGED FORK forming a Y;
cell 4 hub is a SHORT ZIGZAG BAR forming a Z.
Front-facing orthographic with slight visible tops, crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold dark wood, aged honey brass, faint moss at the foot. No lettering of any kind; the hubs are physical metal shapes.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated crank wheels in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
Each crank reads at 16x16 logical pixels but is drawn LARGE and fills its cell. It is a FACE-ON view of a small mechanism wheel standing on the forest floor: a short dark wooden post stub visible only at the bottom edge, a thick worn honey-brass rim around a dark aged-wood wheel face, and a bright raised brass HUB at the dead centre.
The hub is the identifier and must be big, simple and bright: it covers about two thirds of the wheel face, is clearly raised above the wood, and is polished brass with a strong dark outline so it stays readable when the whole sprite is only 16 pixels wide. Value contrast matters more than detail: bright brass against near-black wood.
Cell 1 hub: TWO CROSSED BARS forming an X.
Cell 2 hub: a THREE-PRONGED FORK forming a Y.
Cell 3 hub: a Z-SHAPED BAR with two square bends.
All three share the exact same wheel diameter, rim, post stub, baseline, facing and lighting; only the hub shape changes. Front-facing orthographic, crisp painterly pixel clusters, soft upper-left light, faint moss only on the post stub. No lettering anywhere: each hub is one solid physical metal casting, thick and blocky, not a thin drawn symbol.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated sprites in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor, cast shadow or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
The gate is a NARROW VERTICAL SLIDING LEAF, 8 wide and 40 tall logical pixels, drawn large inside its cell at that tall narrow proportion: dark aged wood planks bound by two thin honey-brass straps, a small square brass keeper plate halfway up, chipped corners. It is NOT an arch, NOT double doors, NOT a portcullis.
Cell 1 GATE CLOSED: the leaf fills the full 8x40 opening, planks tight, straps level, bottom edge seated on a barely visible brass sill.
Cell 2 GATE OPEN: the SAME leaf pulled straight up into its pocket, so the visible part is a compressed gathered bundle at the very top of the cell and the lower four fifths of the cell are COMPLETELY TRANSPARENT empty passage; keep the leaf's outer width identical to cell 1.
Cell 3 LATCH, reading at 8x8 logical pixels but drawn large: a small brass hook lever on a square slate foot, hooked end pointing left over a short steel keeper, a seated pin through the hook. It must read as a mechanical catch that holds a raised gate, not a door handle.
Crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold dark wood, aged honey brass, faint green moss only on the outer edges, soft upper-left light. Same material family and scale across the three.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production 2D game environment plate: a forest floor seen straight top-down, exact wide landscape aspect ratio 608x232, painted at 2x. Painterly pixel-cluster fantasy RPG art, dark blue-green twilight forest, cold moss, wet packed earth, restrained detail.
NO objects and NO props: no steles, no stone blocks, no rings, no cranks, no gate, no walls, no characters, no fireflies, no text, no labels, no UI, no cast shadows of objects, no vignette. This is a floor only.
PATH LAYOUT: a broad worn dirt path enters at the LEFT edge about one third up from the bottom and runs right across the grove. Near the middle it forks: one spur runs UP to a flat trampled stone row along the upper middle where four standing stones will later stand, and one spur runs DOWN into a small open clearing in the lower middle where three cranks will later stand. The main path continues to the RIGHT edge at mid height where a gate will later be. Path edges are soft and worn, with small pebbles, leaf litter and moss creeping in from the sides.
The rest is deep forest floor: dark teal moss, exposed roots, ferns and dense undergrowth along the TOP edge, a few scattered pale flowers, faint dappled light patches. Keep the path unmistakable but LOW contrast and calm, so future props read clearly on top of it. No perspective convergence, flat orthographic ground.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated horizontal axle bars in ONE row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, characters or UI.
Each bar reads at 80x12 logical pixels but is drawn large and wide, lying FLAT ON THE GROUND and seen from directly above: a dark old iron rod with two thick honey-brass collars, one near each end, a few rivets, a slot where it meets a stone base at either end. The middle of each rod is half buried under a thin crust of dark teal moss and fine root fibres, with a couple of dead leaves; the iron shows faint cold highlights where the moss has broken away.
Same rod, same length, same collars, same moss pattern and same lighting in all three cells; they are three copies of one part. Crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold iron, aged honey brass, dark teal moss, soft upper-left light. No glow, no grass blades standing up, no shadow outside the rod.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated brass marks in ONE row, evenly spaced, very generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, letters, arrows or UI.
Each mark reads at 24x24 logical pixels but is drawn large: THIN ENGRAVED LINE ART ONLY, a single-hairline honey-brass drawing with no filled areas and no glow, as if stamped on mossy stone. The mark is a thin open ring with TWO SMALL GLYPHS inside it, side by side, joined by a short horizontal bar between them — the bar is the axle, the two glyphs are the two things it turns.
Cell 1: a small crescent moon on the left joined to a small pointed leaf on the right.
Cell 2: a small pointed leaf on the left joined to a small eight-pointed star on the right.
Cell 3: a small eight-pointed star on the left joined to a small water droplet on the right.
All three share the same ring diameter, line weight, glyph size and spacing; only the glyph pair changes. Same crisp line, same worn brass tone, faint green patina in the grooves. Designed to read when revealed over dark moss.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY TWO isolated props in ONE row, left and right, wide transparent gutter between them, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows or UI.
LEFT PROP, reading at 64x32 logical pixels but drawn large: a SLEEPING HOLLOW at the foot of an old tree, seen front-on and slightly from above. A dark cavity between thick exposed roots, its mouth rimmed with pale worn wood and dark teal moss, a few dry leaves inside, the interior falling into near-black. THREE ADULT FIREFLIES are perched quietly at the rim and just inside it, each a tiny warm amber dot with the faintest one-pixel falloff and one folded wing visible; they are resting, not swarming, and there is no large bloom, no glow cloud and no young larvae.
RIGHT PROP, reading at 16x20 logical pixels but drawn large: a GRASS BELL hanging from a short twig. A small bell woven from dry pale grass blades, a tiny dark wooden clapper showing at the bottom, tied to the twig with a thin cord, one or two blades of grass still attached and curling. Quiet and small, no metal, no shine.
Crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold teal moss, weathered wood, faded straw, warm amber accents only on the fireflies, soft upper-left light. No ground plane, no shadow outside each prop.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game animation strip on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE frames of ONE tiny flying firefly, in a single horizontal row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows or UI.
Each frame reads at 8x8 logical pixels but is drawn large: a warm amber insect with a soft cream glow, a dark tiny body, and thin translucent wings. Frame 1 wings raised, frame 2 wings level and glow brightest, frame 3 wings lowered with the glow slightly dimmer. The three frames must share the exact same body size, glow radius, colour and centre position; only the wings and the glow strength change, so they loop cleanly.
The glow stays tight, about one body width, with no long trails, no sparks and no big bloom. Crisp pixel clusters, warm amber and cream against the transparent background, no green tint, no scenery.
